title: Financial Chart
description: A canvas price chart with candlesticks, area or line and a volume histogram, themed with tokens for light and dark, resizing with its container, with a keyboard cursor and a spoken summary, over Lightweight Charts.

props.name: data
props.type: { time, open, high, low, close, volume? }[]
props.description: One entry per period, in time order. `time` is a "YYYY-MM-DD" string, a UNIX timestamp in seconds or a business day object. Area and line draw the close.

props.name: volume
props.default: true when any datum has a volume
props.description: A volume histogram under the price (bottom 30%; price in the top 60%), each bar colored by its period's direction.

props.name: volumeScale
props.description: "auto" is the library's default: the volume scale fits the bars' own range, so small differences look large. "zero" starts it at zero so bar heights are proportional to volume (the demo uses it).

props.name: height
props.description: Height in pixels; the width follows the container and the chart resizes with it.

props.name: summary
props.description: The description read after the name. By default: the period range, first and last close with the change, the high and the low.

props.name: dataTable
props.description: Also renders every point in a visually hidden table.

props.name: options
props.description: Any lightweight-charts chart option (scales, crosshair, localization, handleScroll), applied over the token colors. Keep `layout.attributionLogo` on (see a11y and docs).

props.name: seriesOptions
props.description: Style options for the price series (for example `priceFormat`, `lineWidth`), applied over the token colors.

props.name: ref
props.description: `getChart()`, `getSeries()`, `getVolumeSeries()` (the library's own APIs, for markers, price lines or live `update()`), and `showPoint(index | null)` to place the crosshair.

a11y: The chart is a figure named by `label` and described by a generated summary (range, first and last close with the change, high and low), or by `summary`. `dataTable` adds every point as a visually hidden table.

Keyboard: the chart is one Tab stop, a slider over the points. Left and Right (or Down and Up) move the crosshair one point, Page Up and Page Down ten, Home and End to the ends; each point is read out (time, open, high, low, close, volume) as the slider's value text. The focus ring is drawn over the chart; pointer input goes straight to the chart.
The library lays its panes out in an HTML table; the wrapper marks it as presentation, so it is not announced as a data table. The canvases carry no text of their own.

Attribution: the library's license asks for a visible link to its author's website. The chart keeps lightweight-charts' attribution logo on (`layout.attributionLogo`, the default): a small logo link at the bottom left, named by its title ("Charting by TradingView"), opening in a new tab. Do not turn it off unless the same link is shown elsewhere on the page.
Reduced motion: touch kinetic scrolling is off under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The chart has no other animation.
Right to left: the plot stays left to right (time runs left to right in every language); the summary and labels follow the page.
Colors: up and down are also told apart by shape (a candle's open and close, the summary's signed change), not by color alone. The default text #191919 on white is 17:1.
usage:
<FinancialChart
  label="Sample asset, daily prices"
  data={candles}
  series="candlestick"
/>
